- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply a “cool-down” penalty: subtract 3–8% from forecast 2–3 periods after peak.
- If sentiment is uniformly positive (≥0.9) and price is trending up, model overreacts; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent high.
- If sentiment turns negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 20–40% in subsequent periods.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% per period until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the window; apply a “lag correction”: subtract 1–3% from first 5–7 forecast points.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to underestimate; add 2–5% to forecast to counteract bias.
